name: MALDIVES

flag.title: Flag of Maldives
flag.note: Green panel, white crescent on red field

lead: The Maldives is a necklace of coral islands in the Indian Ocean, south-west of Sri Lanka. About 1,190 tiny islands form 26 atolls. All the land would fit inside a medium-sized city. It is the flattest country on Earth.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: One of world's most crowded cities

facts.label: Language
facts.sub: Thaana script, reads right to left

facts.label: Land area
facts.sub: Smallest country in Asia by land

sections.geography: A chain of tiny coral crowns

geo: The Maldives sits on a long underwater ridge. All the islands are coral and sand. None rises more than a few metres above the sea.
The country spreads over 90,000 km² of ocean, but its land is only 298 km². On average islands sit less than 1.5 m above the waves.
animals: The national animal is the yellowfin tuna. Fishers have caught it for centuries with one pole and one line. Over 1,000 fish species live on the reefs.
Whale sharks, the biggest fish on Earth, cruise the warm waters. Five kinds of sea turtle nest here.
culture: Bodu Beru means 'big drum'. Drummers start slowly and build to a fast, trance-like beat while dancers spin. The rhythm came with African sailors around the 11th century.
Fish appears at almost every meal. Garudhiya is a clear tuna broth with rice, lime and chilli. The wooden dhoni boat has linked the islands for over a thousand years.
history: People have lived in the Maldives for 2,500 years. In 1153 the islands turned to Islam. Sultans then ruled for over 800 years.
Portugal seized Malé in 1558 but was driven out 15 years later. Britain made the islands a protectorate in 1887. Independence came on 26 July 1965 and a republic on 11 November 1968.
wows: The highest point is only 5.1 m, about as tall as a giraffe.
Waves glow electric blue at night on Vaadhoo Island, where plankton flash light.
In 2009 the cabinet held a meeting underwater.
Maldivian cowrie shells were used as money across Africa and Asia.
With no rivers or hills, the Maldives gets fresh water from rain.
All the land of the Maldives is smaller than Seoul.
In 2008 the Maldives planned to buy land abroad in case seas rise.

myths.myth: The Maldives will vanish underwater soon
myths.fact: Seas are rising, but studies found most islands stable or growing. People also build up land, like Hulhumalé.
Resorts are pricey. But guesthouses on local islands show the same reefs for much less.
